title: Two Nobel Winners Lost $4.6 Billion in 4 Months #shorts
description:
In 1998, a hedge fund run by Wall Street legends and two Nobel Prize winners lost $4.6 billion in less than four months, and the Federal Reserve had to step in.
The story of Long-Term Capital Management.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
first_comment: If two Nobel winners couldn't beat the market with all that math, can anyone? 👇

lines.text: In 1998, two Nobel Prize winners lost four point six billion dollars in less than four months.
And they almost took Wall Street down with them.
The fund was called Long-Term Capital Management.
Its partners included the economists who had just won the Nobel Prize for pricing options.
Their math found tiny gaps between prices. So they borrowed huge sums to make them pay.
For every dollar they had, they bet about twenty-five.
At first, it worked. Investors made around forty percent a year.
Then, in August 1998, Russia stopped paying its debts.
Markets panicked, and every bet moved the wrong way at once.
The fund was bleeding hundreds of millions a day.
If it collapsed, the shock could hit banks around the world.
So the Federal Reserve called fourteen banks into one room. They put in three point six billion dollars to stop the fall.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
